name: humanizer
description: Agent skill that removes signs of AI-generated writing from text
one_liner: A free tool that rewrites AI-generated text so it stops sounding robotic — killing the em-dashes, forced 'not just X, it's Y' phrasing, and other AI writing tells — without changing what it actually says.
buyer: A content marketer, student, or small-business owner who publishes AI-assisted writing (blog posts, emails, LinkedIn posts) and is worried it reads as obviously AI-written or gets flagged.
business_use_cases: A content marketing agency runs every AI-drafted blog post through it before publishing, protecting clients' brand voice and SEO reputation.
A student or job-seeker uses it to clean up AI-assisted cover letters and essays so they read as genuinely personal.
A newsletter writer feeds it 2-3 paragraphs of their own past writing to match their voice, cutting editing time on every AI-drafted issue.

money_ideas.idea: Wrap it in a simple web UI (paste text, get humanized text back) and charge a small monthly fee for non-technical users who don't want to install a coding agent.
Sell it as a plugin/add-on inside existing writing tools (Notion, Google Docs) via a one-time license.

steal_this: Build a no-signup web page this weekend: paste AI text in, get de-AI'd text out, powered by this skill's pattern list, and monetize with a simple usage-based API tier for power users.
